meta.tagline: The gastronomy capital of pistachios, copper and mosaics

overview.title: Welcome to Gaziantep
overview.intro: You arrive in Gaziantep hungry and leave with a full heart: this is UNESCO's city of gastronomy, the homeland of baklava, the academy of kebab and the capital of the pistachio. But Antep is not only a table — the world-famous mosaics of Zeugma, the coppersmiths' hammers ringing around the castle, six-hundred-year-old caravanserais and Turkey's oldest coffeehouse all live in these streets. At this stop on the Silk Road, the old etiquette of trade survives: the shopkeeper offers tea, the master shows his work, and the table is always shared.

local_word.definition: The Antep pistachio: this city's gold, pride and unit of measure. It gives baklava its green, ice cream its crown, and conversation its snack. Locals grade it by 'boz iç' (the prized young kernel) and treat the harvest as a festival — leaving without pistachios is like leaving the sea without touching water.

rules.title: Start the day with beyran
rules.description: The official opening of an Antep morning is beyran: in halls that open at 06:00, garlicky, spicy lamb slow-cooked in bone broth awaits you. Don't resist the idea of 'soup for breakfast' — drink it once and you'll understand why Antep mornings start early.

rules.title: Eat baklava in the morning, from a master
rules.description: True Antep baklava is eaten fresh off the morning tray: the pistachio green, the pastry crackling, the butter fresh. Believe the master who says 'cold baklava is leftover baklava' — the 08:00 tray and the afternoon tray are not the same dessert.

rules.title: Don't rush the bazaar, never refuse the tea
rules.description: The coppersmiths' bazaar and the caravanserai district are not a shopping mall but a living school of craft: talk to the master, listen to the hammer's rhythm. A shopkeeper's offer of tea is not a sales tactic, it's Antep etiquette — accept it, chat, and then buy nothing if you like.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: The Antep manner is warm and generous

tip.label: The Antep philosophy
tip.text: In this city the itinerary is built around the stomach: beyran at dawn, kebab at noon, katmer in the afternoon, with museums sprinkled in between. Eat little and often — Antep is not a marathon but a long, unhurried feast.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The airport is close to the center and the historic core is walkable; Zeugma and Rumkale call for wheels.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: Gaziantep Airport is twenty minutes from the center: shuttle services and taxis run steadily. Frequent flights arrive from Istanbul, Ankara and Izmir — the ideal distance for a weekend gastronomy escape.

items.title: A walkable historic core
items.description: The castle, the coppersmiths' bazaar, the caravanserais and the Bey quarter are all within walking distance: historic Antep can be paced in half a day. Comfortable shoes for the stone pavements — bazaar breaks stretch the walk on their own.

items.title: Tram and buses
items.description: The tram line runs from the university to the center, and buses weave the city: a Gaziantepkart covers both. Short taxi hops between center and museums are effortless too — distances in this city are small.

items.title: Wheels for Zeugma and beyond
items.description: The Zeugma Mosaic Museum is ten minutes from the center: easily reached by taxi or bus. For the Rumkale and Halfeti escape you'll need a rental car or a day tour — the road rewards you with Euphrates views.

items.title: Walking the bazaar labyrinth
items.description: From Zincirli Bedesten to the Bone Bedesten, from Sire Han to Kurkcu Han, the bazaars interlock: getting lost is part of the program. Follow the sound of hammers — the coppersmiths' quarter is the bazaar's heart.

callout.label: Museum tip
callout.text: Go to Zeugma at morning opening: you'll stand eye to eye with the Gypsy Girl without the crowds. Give the museum at least two hours — mosaics don't like haste, and the lit halls are at their emptiest in the morning.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: The choice in Antep is twofold: a stone-mansion boutique in the historic core, or a comfortable hotel in the new city — ten minutes apart.

local_word.definition: The courtyarded stone inns where Silk Road caravans once lodged: the backbone of the Antep bazaar. Some still trade, others became cafes and boutique hotels — drinking tea in their courtyards is taking a seat in six hundred years of commerce.

items.name: Bey quarter (Bey Mahallesi)
items.description: The neighborhood of stone mansions: carved doors, courtyard boutique hotels, museum-houses. The address for waking up inside historic Antep — walking distance to the bazaar and the castle.

items.name: Castle and bazaar district
items.description: The beyran halls, baklava houses and caravanserai district at your doorstep: you can stroll to the 06:00 beyran in your slippers. The most practical base for a gastronomy-first visit.

items.name: Ibrahimli and the new center
items.description: Modern hotels with big rooms and parking: a strong price-to-comfort balance. Ten minutes by taxi to the historic core — the new city's evening cafes are here too.

items.name: Around the station
items.description: A practical district near the bus terminal and main arteries: sensible for short stays and early departures. The center is a few tram stops away.

items.name: Kavaklik
items.description: A quiet district known for its parks: the local choice for family visits and noiseless nights. A short taxi to the center — an evening walk in Kavaklik park is a pleasure.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: The Antep table is open in all four seasons; the pistachio harvest calls for autumn, spice scents for spring, and hot summer middays for courtyard shade.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Spiced Spring
items.subtitle: Spring · Mild bazaar days, fresh greens on the table
items.description: The sweetest season for bazaar wandering: mild air, cool courtyards, tables brightened with spring onions and purslane. In May the Antep kitchen shifts to its spring menu with new-harvest vegetables — the walk-and-eat balance is easiest to strike in these months.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May the cig kofte and fresh-greens tables peak: walk the Bey quarter in the evening cool and drink menengic coffee in a mansion courtyard. The museum-bazaar-table triangle runs like clockwork this month.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Courtyard Shade Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Hot middays, cool han courtyards
items.description: Antep summer is hot: midday belongs to museums and han courtyards, morning and evening to the bazaar. Watermelon with cheese, kunefe with ice cream — the summer table adapts too. Air-conditioned Zeugma is the most elegant escape from the noon heat.

callout.label: Midday note
callout.text: In July–August, street wandering between 12:00 and 16:00 is a struggle: give those hours to Zeugma, the Emine Gogus museum or a han courtyard break. At 09:00 the bazaar is both cool and calm.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Pistachio Harvest
items.subtitle: Autumn · Boz iç time, drying-rack bustle
items.description: September is the month of the pistachio harvest: the stalls fill with the new crop, and peppers and eggplants redden on the rooftop drying lines. The weather softens, the bazaar quickens — this is Antep at its most Antep.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: In harvest season, ask the nut seller for 'boz iç' pistachios: tasting the new crop's fresh green is the privilege of the year. You'll feel the difference at the katmer counter too — katmer opens differently when the pistachio is at its greenest.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Beyran Season
items.subtitle: Winter · Steaming halls, ember-side conversations
items.description: On a cold Antep morning, the steam of a beyran hall is the most inviting sight in town: winter is the season of this kitchen's heavy artillery. Yuvalama, kebab off the embers, hot katmer — tourists thin out, the table returns to the locals, and conversation stretches long.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: The 07:00 winter beyran is a ritual: the hall in steam, the spoons in rhythm. Ask for the garlic and chili 'full strength' — this is Antep's six-hundred-year-old answer to the cold.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: This is Turkey's gastronomy capital: you need not a list but a curriculum — start with beyran, finish with katmer, and entrust the middle to kebab and baklava.

local_word.definition: The Antep breakfast where lamb slow-cooked for hours in bone broth meets rice, plenty of garlic and red pepper in a boiling cauldron: drunk at 06:00, it carries you through the day. To a local it's not soup but an institution — the phrase 'like beyran' describes anything solid and full-hearted.

items.name: Beyran
items.description: The morning's boiling overture: bone broth, shredded lamb, garlic and heat. Drunk in the hall to the sound of spoons, with pickles and bread alongside — the first spoonful is a lesson, the second a habit.
items.tag: 06:00 ritual · ask for it full strength

items.name: Antep baklava
items.description: Forty layers of pastry, boz iç pistachios, fresh butter: in baklava's homeland, the morning tray is a league of its own. Ask the master about the 'dry' and 'moist' styles — pastry that folds like a towel is the good sign itself.
items.tag: Off the morning tray · pistachio green

items.name: The kebab curriculum
items.description: From Ali Nazik to kusleme, simit kebab to onion kebab: Antep kebab is not a list but a school. If your visit lands in season, don't miss the loquat and garlic kebabs — the embers keep a seasonal calendar.
items.tag: A menu like a school · ask for the season's kebab

items.name: Yuvalama and icli kofte
items.description: Yuvalama, the festival soup of tiny chickpea-yogurt dumplings, and icli kofte, elegant bulgur shells with spiced filling: Antep home cooking speaks through these two plates. Look for a home-style lokanta.

items.name: Katmer
items.description: Clotted cream, pistachio and sugar in paper-thin pastry: the morning's sweet contender, baklava's young rival. Eaten hot at the counter — asking for 'double pistachio' is a declaration of love in Antep.
items.tag: Hot off the counter · cream and double pistachio

items.name: Menengic coffee and the nut stall
items.description: Menengic is the wild terebinth pistachio, ember-roasted and brewed with milk: its scent is the bazaar's memory. Fresh boz iç from the nut seller alongside — this is Antep's hospitality duo.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: In Antep, quietly walk away from anywhere with a 'tourist menu': a good hall's menu is short and its plates are deep. Ask the master 'what should I eat today?' — in Antep that question is a mark of respect, and the answer never misleads.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees Zeugma and the castle; these six are Antep's hidden face, ringing with hammers and scented with coffee.

items.name: Tahmis Kahvesi
items.description: A wooden-columned hall where coffee has brewed since the 1630s: menengic on the embers, conversation at full volume, history at every table. A cup at this ancient counter is a seat in the city's memory.

items.name: Bey Mahallesi
items.description: Carved doors, courtyard mansions, museum-houses: the stone streets of old Antep's merchant class. Break in a mansion courtyard cafe — the walls tell stories in the Antep dialect.

items.name: The coppersmith masters
items.description: The tinner's bellows, the hammer's rhythm, blackened aprons: copper is still beaten by hand here. Buy at least a cezve from a master — one who shows you his work won't withhold his tea either.

items.name: Zincirli Bedesten
items.description: A covered bazaar from the 1700s: spice sellers, kutnu fabric merchants and dried-vegetable stalls under stone arches. In the morning hours, the shopkeepers' conversation is worth more than the shopping.

items.name: Rumkale and Halfeti
items.description: An hour away, a boat on the green water of the Euphrates: half-sunken Halfeti and the fortress of Rumkale on its rocky headland. A submerged minaret, black rose legends and river coolness — Antep's water side.

items.name: Emine Gogus Culinary Museum
items.description: An encyclopedia of the Antep kitchen in a stone mansion: copper cookware, century-old recipes, the etiquette of the tray table. Once you know the dishes' stories, the table tastes different — come before your bazaar tour and eat knowing what you eat.

callout.label: Bazaar strategy
callout.text: Walk the caravanserai district between 09:00 and 11:00: shutters freshly opened, masters at work, tea stoves boiling. Move to a museum in the midday heat — the late-afternoon return to the bazaar is shopping's golden hour.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Gastronomic fame invites imitation; know these four games and you'll eat the real Antep.

items.name: The tourist baklava box
items.description: In some windows the 'Antep baklava' label is stuck on stale stock or mass production short on pistachio; the gift-box price outruns the real thing.
items.instead: Buy from the morning tray, by weight, after tasting: a good baklava house never hesitates to offer a taste. Look for green pistachio and the scent of butter — the tray's freshness speaks, not the box's packaging.

items.name: The long-menu 'kebab palaces'
items.description: A hundred-item tourist menu signals the freezer, not the embers; the waiter's 'special' is usually the most expensive line.
items.instead: Choose masters with short menus and halls full of locals: order by saying 'whatever the master recommends'. A customer who asks about the season's kebab is taken seriously in the kitchen.

items.name: Machine-pressed 'hand-beaten' copper
items.description: At some stalls, press-made goods sell at hand-beaten prices; a bright polish often hides mass production.
items.instead: Look for hammer marks on the inner surface and buy from the master's own workshop: beaten copper's marks are irregular and its ring is deep. A master who shows you the making quotes an honest price too.

items.name: The noon baklava-and-beyran plan
items.description: Beyran at noon and baklava in the afternoon means tasting both in the second league — beyran belongs to the morning cauldron, baklava to the morning tray.
items.instead: Set your stomach to Antep time: beyran at 07:00, baklava at 09:00, kebab at noon, katmer in the afternoon. The early riser wins twice in this city — both the freshness and the queue belong to the morning person.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Antep, wherever the crowd is local is an unfailing compass: look at the hall, not the sign. If shopkeepers are eating somewhere, you can sit down — in this city, the tradesman's stomach is the strictest critic.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From beyran to katmer — a gastronomy day

steps.title: Beyran overture
steps.description: Start the day in a steaming hall: garlicky, spicy, bone-broth deep. You'll understand at the first spoonful — this city takes mornings seriously.

steps.title: Morning baklava
steps.description: Baklava fresh off the tray with tea: pistachio green, pastry crackling. Buy by weight, eat at the counter — save the box for evening gifts.

steps.title: Castle and the coppersmiths' bazaar
steps.description: Walk from the castle toward the sound of hammers: the masters' workshops, the arches of Zincirli Bedesten, the scent of spices. Don't refuse the tea.

steps.title: Kebab noon
steps.description: Ali Nazik or the day's kebab at a short-menu master: 'whatever the master recommends' is the truest order. Charred peppers alongside.

steps.title: Zeugma Mosaic Museum
steps.description: Eye to eye with the Gypsy Girl: give two hours to one of the world's great mosaic collections. The most elegant escape from the afternoon heat.

steps.title: Bey quarter and the katmer finale
steps.description: An evening walk among the stone mansions, menengic coffee at Tahmis, and hot katmer to close — don't forget to say 'double pistachio'.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Table, craft and the Euphrates — the full Antep

steps.title: Classic Antep
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: beyran, morning baklava, the bazaar, kebab, Zeugma, the Bey quarter and katmer.

steps.title: Craft and kitchen depth
steps.description: Morning theory of the Antep table at the Emine Gogus Culinary Museum; a home-style lunch of yuvalama and icli kofte; late-afternoon caravanserai tour — Sire Han, Kurkcu Han, the kutnu fabric looms; evening of long conversation at Tahmis Kahvesi.

steps.title: Euphrates escape
steps.description: Set out in the morning and reach Halfeti in an hour: a boat past the submerged minaret and Rumkale on the Euphrates; riverside fish for lunch; on the way back, boz iç pistachios and a baklava box from the nut seller — let the suitcase smell of Antep.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: The Antep manner is generous and heart-winning; these five phrases open doors at the table and in the bazaar.

items.meaning: 'Welcome' — the first phrase you'll hear at the hall door and in the han courtyard
The Antep-style invitation — 'gardaş' is the warm word for brother; smile when you hear it
'Enjoy your meal' — opens and closes every table from beyran to katmer
'Health to your hands' — the most precious thank-you to a master, said to kebab cooks and coppersmiths alike
'Make the pistachio double' — the password of the katmer counter; Antep's sweet measure of generosity

checklist.completion_message: Ellerine sağlık! You've lived the gastronomy capital the way it deserves!
